before.rationale: Provisionally, the Upper East Side's residential base may support repeat dining and delivery demand at lower assumed rents than SoHo, which suits a cuisine with strong takeout appeal. This rests on unverified assumptions about rent, competition and concept, and whether to open at all is undetermined without financial and demand data.

after.rationale: Synthetic-panel signals are mixed: SoHo personas reported somewhat higher frequency and more dissatisfaction (a possible gap), while Upper East Side personas indicated higher price tolerance and a resident-heavy base. With tiny, unevenly composed AI-persona groups and no rent or competition data, the evidence is insufficient to overturn the provisional choice, and whether to open at all remains undetermined.

changedAssumptions.before: SoHo traffic skews toward tourists and shoppers, while the Upper East Side skews toward residents who dine out and order delivery repeatedly.
changedAssumptions.after: SoHo demand may skew toward workers and visitors with lower per-meal price expectations (e.g., lunch), while the Upper East Side may skew toward residents with higher price tolerance; the synthetic panel did not show higher Indian-food frequency on the Upper East Side, and this remains an unverified assumption.

supporting: q3: 6 of 14 Upper East Side personas expected $35 or more per main versus 2 of 15 SoHo personas, suggesting higher price tolerance.
q1: Upper East Side personas were mostly residents (12 of 14), loosely consistent with a repeat, resident-driven customer base.
q5: Delivery and convenience (22 mentions) and consistent quality (24) were top themes, fitting a reliable neighborhood delivery-oriented concept.
contradicting: q2: 11 of 15 SoHo personas ate Indian food at least monthly versus 8 of 14 Upper East Side personas.
q4: 6 of 15 SoHo personas were dissatisfied with current options versus 3 of 14 on the Upper East Side, hinting at a possibly underserved SoHo market.
q5: Demand for lunch specials and deals under $15 suggests a worker-heavy SoHo lunch opportunity a fast-casual concept could capture.
limitations: Responses come from 30 AI-generated personas, not real people, and are directional only.
Neighborhood subgroups are tiny (15 and 14) and mix residents and workers very differently, confounding neighborhood comparisons.
The run was uncalibrated and demographics beyond gender were invented by the generator.
Q5 theme counts could not be filtered to this specific run.
Stated frequency and price are not observed spending.
Rents, competitive density and the founder's concept and capital were not studied, so the go/no-go question is unresolved.

confidenceBefore.reason: The recommendation relies entirely on unverified assumptions about rent, demand, competition and concept, with no data provided.

confidenceAfter.reason: Synthetic, small-sample signals point in mixed directions and key factors like rent and competition remain unstudied.
